text.p: Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Tuesday it expected its 1997 earnings to be similar to the 1996 level, with profit before extras earlier reported at 3.56 billion markka.
"At present UPM-Kymmene expects the financial result for 1997 to be similar to that for last year," the company said in a statement with its results.
Economic growth was expected to increase gradually in Europe, the company's main market, and this would increase paper consumption, UPM said.
"Deliveries of printing and writing papers are expected to be up on 1996, although sales prices will be lower, at least in the early part of the year," it said.
Printing paper prices have probably bottomed out, it said.

"Better demand early in 1997 has raised capacity utilisation rates and paved the way for an increase in sales prices," UPM said. "It is hoped to raise fine paper and LWC prices during the first quarter of the year," it added.
At the start of 1997, sawn timber prices were well up on 1996, and consumption of sawn timber and plywood was expected to be higher than last year, UPM-Kymmene said.
Group gross capital expenditure was expected to be around six billion markka this year with the biggest investment being a new LWC paper machine for the Rauma paper mill, UPM said.
